messages:
dani: Ran into a weird onboarding loop on my new M1 macbook. Installed redwoodctl via Homebrew, did `redwoodctl auth login` and the browser returned success but `redwoodctl whoami` says 'not logged in'.

priya: Hmm. Which Homebrew path did you use? On M1 there are two prefixes (/opt/homebrew vs /usr/local) and some installers write config to the wrong home.

dani: Brew default is /opt/homebrew. I inspected `~/.config/redwood` and it's empty. Found token under `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/redwoodctl/1.2.3/libexec/.config/redwood/token.json`. CLI isn't reading that.

priya: Likely the formula executed a postinstall as the brew owner and wrote to its own libexec. Short term fix: copy token to your XDG config dir: `mkdir -p ~/.config/redwood && cp /opt/homebrew/Cellar/redwoodctl/1.2.3/libexec/.config/redwood/token.json ~/.config/redwood/`

ops-bot: NOTE: filed GH#889 (packaging: brew formula writes token to libexec path; prefer user XDG path or offer --token-path).

packaging: We saw this before when the postinstall runs under a different user. We should change the formula to avoid auto-writing tokens and instead print a postinstall message instructing users to run `redwoodctl auth login` themselves. Also add `--token-path` so automation can write to a specified path.

priya: Agreed. Also adding `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` env var + `--config-dir` flag will help constrained installs and packaging variants (brew, snap, flatpak). We'll also add a small diagnostic `auth status` that prints where the CLI read tokens from when present.

dani: Copying token to ~/.config fixed it and `redwoodctl whoami` now shows my email. Will help test the packaging PR if you want.

priya: Thanks. For now I'll update the Homebrew formula notes and add the postinstall message: "If auth fails after install, run `redwoodctl auth login` or copy token into ~/.config/redwood/`". Also linking to the headless token example for CI.

dani: Happy to validate the formula change. Also: can we add a tiny CLI hint when we detect a token in a nonstandard libexec path, e.g., "Found token at /opt/homebrew/... but not in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME; copying or passing --config-dir may help" ?

packaging: Good idea, low-friction. We'll aim for that in the next release.
thread_text: Installed redwoodctl via Homebrew on M1, browser auth reported success but CLI still says 'not logged in' because token ended up in brew libexec path instead of ~/.config/redwood.
